name: openedai-speech
description: OpenAI-compatible TTS proxy (POST /v1/audio/speech) wrapping Coqui XTTS v2, Piper, and Kokoro backends; commonly bundled in self-hosted LLM stacks alongside Ollama and Open-WebUI; no authentication layer in any version; archived upstream January 2026 with no patches forthcoming
auth_notes: Zero authentication in all deployment configurations. The OpenAIStub base class (openedai.py) registers no auth middleware whatsoever. Arbitrary bearer tokens (e.g., sk-111111111) are accepted and silently ignored — no validation occurs. CORS middleware is configured with allow_origins:["*"], allow_credentials:True, allow_methods:["*"], allow_headers:["*"] — completely permissive. No rate limiting, no IP allowlisting, no token scoping. Official integration docs explicitly instruct users to enter a dummy API key because the server does not require one. Repository archived 2026-01-04; no authentication mechanism has ever shipped and none will.

shodan_dorks.rationale: Matches the /v1/models JSON response body containing the tts-1-hd model ID; specific to openedai-speech and compatible forks on the default port
Conjunctive match on owned_by:openedai field in /v1/models JSON plus tts-1 model name; narrows to canonical matatonic deployments and direct forks

Combines the billing stub artifact (total_usage:0 from /v1/billing/usage and /v1/dashboard/billing/usage) with the HD TTS model name; both are synthetic OpenAIStub responses that co-occur only in openedai-speech-derived servers
Alternate port used when openedai-speech is bundled behind nginx or in multi-service stacks alongside Ollama or Open-WebUI
Targets instances where the TTS endpoint path appears in an error page, docs fragment, or indexed response body alongside the model name; port-agnostic for stack deployments

risk_notes: Unauth compute abuse: POST /v1/audio/speech accepts arbitrary text and synthesizes audio with no access control; GPU-equipped instances (XTTS v2, 4GB VRAM) can be exhausted or weaponized for bulk TTS generation. Voice cloning: XTTS v2 tts-1-hd model supports voice cloning from a 6-30 second mono WAV sample — unauth access enables targeted impersonation audio for vishing, CEO fraud, or deepfake audio dataset construction. CSRF: fully open CORS (allow_origins:*) allows any browser-originating cross-site request to generate audio from a victim's co-located server without user interaction. Resource exhaustion DoS: no rate limiting on TTS generation; GPU or CPU can be saturated. /v1/billing/usage returns {"total_usage":0} — attacker can confirm service is operational without triggering any metering. Lateral movement: co-deployment in Ollama/Open-WebUI stacks means a compromised or exposed openedai-speech instance may share Docker network segments with the LLM inference backend. Archived repo: Coqui XTTS v2, Piper, and FastAPI/uvicorn dependency vulnerabilities will never receive patches from upstream.
deployment_notes: Default deployment is Docker Compose on port 8000:8000 with restart:unless-stopped. Server binds 0.0.0.0 by default. Full CUDA image (ghcr.io/matatonic/openedai-speech, ~8GB) requires Nvidia Docker runtime and ~4GB VRAM for XTTS v2. Minimal CPU-only variant (ghcr.io/matatonic/openedai-speech-min, ~860MB) runs Piper only. ROCm variant targets AMD GPUs. ARM64 builds support Apple M-series and Raspberry Pi. Config loaded from speech.env and config/voice_to_speaker.yaml; both are hot-reloadable without restart. Voice models downloaded from HuggingFace on first use (HF_HOME=voices). Commonly deployed as TTS sidecar in Ollama + Open-WebUI stacks, exposing the service at http://host.docker.internal:8000/v1. Repository archived 2026-01-04 — upstream is frozen; Coqui dependency itself has also been archived, compounding supply-chain risk. Active successor projects include speaches (speaches.ai) and kokoro-fastapi.
